decision.title: Regular expressions: hand-written parser, compiled regex and matcher (packet )

body.p: . The regex text is parsed by a hand-written recursive-descent parser in src/regex.c, not by a tree-sitter grammar: an exception to , for these reasons. (1) A regex is run-time data, compiled during evaluation (fn:tokenize($s, $p) with a computed $p), and tree-sitter allocates with malloc outside every sxml allocator and limit ( accepts that only for the parse step of source text). (2) The flags change the lexing before any grammar applies (F&O 4.0, section 6.2: x removes whitespace except inside [...], c removes #...# comments, q makes every character literal), so a grammar would need a preprocessing pass that is most of a parser. (3) Tokens are single characters whose meaning depends on context (inside or outside [...], after \, the hyphen rules of XSD 1.1), and back-references need the groups closed so far; a context-free grammar plus a tree walk adds a layer without removing any check. (4) FORX0002 needs a precise reason, and tree-sitter ERROR nodes give none. (5) Saxon HE and regexml, the models of , parse by hand too. The XSD dialect (Phase 5) is a flag of the same parser. Interface (src/regex_internal.h), which the engine keeps: sxml_regex_parse_flags (FORX0001); sxml_regex, compiled from and flags, immutable, shareable between threads, with the lifecycle of (memory requirements found by a counting pass of the parser, so they are exact and need no scratch memory); sxml_regex_matcher, the per-thread working state (backtrack stack through an allocator, captured groups, step count), with match_at (anchored), find (first matching segment at or after an offset) and find_next (the next of the disjoint matching segments, F&O 4.0, section 6.1.1), each writing an sxml_regex_search_result (found or not, and the segment: the bool outputs the lint forbids become a struct), and captured groups as byte ranges of the regex input. Positions are byte offsets at codepoint boundaries. A regex error is SXML_STATUS_DYNAMIC_ERROR with err:FORX0002 in the error record the configuration points to; running out of steps or stack is SXML_STATUS_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, not a spec error. The seed () supports: literals, ., classes with ranges, negation and subtraction, \s \S \d \D \w \W (Unicode 16.0 tables generated by tools/generate-regex-tables.py), greedy and reluctant quantifiers, capturing and non-capturing groups, alternation, ^ $, back-references, and flags s m i x q c. FORX0002 with "not supported by the regex seed": \p \P \i \I \c \C \b \B, lookahead and lookbehind, named groups and \k; with i, non-ASCII characters in the regex and back-references (case variants beyond ASCII need Unicode case data). A public step limit in sxml_processor_limits is left for the packet (a new field).

No recursion (), amended 2026-10-16: the parser reads pieces in one loop and keeps open groups on an explicit stack of group frames, inline for SXML_REGEX_INLINE_GROUP_DEPTH (16) groups, then grown through the new stack_allocator of sxml_regex_configuration and released before the call returns (sxml_regex_create uses its own allocator; without one, deeper nesting is CAPACITY_EXCEEDED); maximum_group_depth (default 100) now bounds that heap. Every atom is parsed and emitted once: a "|" inserts the split of the branch before it, a quantifier inserts what precedes the first copy and appends copies of the atom's instructions (targets moved, progress registers renumbered, classes shared), so the lexical skipping and re-parsing are gone. Class subtraction is a chain, read and matched in loops. Arrays are sized by the most a pass wrote, which fixes a write past the arrays when an atom quantified with {0} came last ((ab){0} at the end). 400,000 random regexes compile, fail and match exactly as before.
